text: ICE's median rate per detention bed per day in fiscal year 2026: $92.
Median rate per bed per day at the eight Bureau of Prisons sites ICE uses: $182, about double ICE's median.
Rate per bed per day that FEMA's grant allows for Florida's soft-sided (tent) site: $249, about 171% above ICE's median.

People held on an average day rose from 39,314 on January 20, 2025 to 67,180 on July 30, 2026, up 71% (GAO's figure; ICE's own detention file, used elsewhere on this page, gives a slightly lower count for early August).
Detention sites ICE is authorized to use roughly doubled, from 134 to 272.
ICE spent more than $2.5 billion buying warehouses and existing facilities as of July 2026, including about $1.07 billion for 11 warehouses and about $1.5 billion for two facilities.

GAO found waste: about $7.1 million for meals ICE did not need at Camp East Montana (October 2025 to March 2026), $2.85 million of tents at Guantánamo that were never used, and $7.7 million that cannot be recovered on seven warehouses ICE plans to sell.
